headline: Ukraine's former defense minister launched a 'Manhattan Project' for killer robots, as six AI companies signed a 'morally binding' White House safety accord and the FTC opened a probe into OpenAI and Anthropic over safety risks.

points.text: Six major AI companies signed a voluntary, 'morally binding' AI safety accord with the White House after a meeting with Trump; commentators questioned how much the non-binding agreement actually changes.

Ukraine's former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov launched a 'Manhattan Project'-style program for killer robots, saying he wants humanoid-like robots on the battlefield within six months and an infantry-free assault within a year.
The Federal Trade Commission is investigating OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies over potential safety risks posed by their products.
METR president Chris Painter testified before a US Senate subcommittee on AI agent incidents.
OpenAI said it disrupted a coordinated campaign to extract its protected model reasoning through distillation, and is strengthening defenses against such attacks.
The Pentagon's War Department said it is working with industry partners to deploy the latest US AI models and platforms across government.
Google unveiled its next frontier model, Gemini 4 Argon, but is initially restricting access to a small group of 'trusted cyber defenders.'
The Trump administration's new AI chatbot gave inconsistent answers to politically sensitive questions, including about the 2020 election, sometimes answering and sometimes refusing.
